# Vendored winit fork

Source: https://github.com/storytold/winit rev a517b3846ee8457d84ee4975110bfda6797c44dc (Apache-2.0). Unmodified sources, `docs/` dropped.

## Local patch: iOS UIScene (iOS 27 SDK)
Backport of molenick/winit@94d6a23 (rust-windowing/winit PR #4723, open, Apache-2.0): features `UIScene`/`UIWindowScene` in `Cargo.toml`, `os_capabilities().scenes` in `ios/app_state.rs`, and `ios/window.rs` attaches the new `UIWindow` to the connected `UIWindowScene`. The commit alone is not enough: the app Info.plist must declare `UIApplicationSceneManifest` with a `UISceneConfigurations`/`UIWindowSceneSessionRoleApplication` entry (no scene delegate), as in `packaging/ios/Info*.plist`; without it UIKit still aborts with "UIScene life cycle is required". Windows are created in `Resumed` (didBecomeActive), after the scene has connected, so the later PR head's deferral of `can_create_surfaces` was not needed. Drop it when a winit release contains #4723.

## Local patch: iOS UITextInput (CJK composition, autocorrection, candidate position)
Base: rust-windowing/winit PR #4592 (open, head e49d771a, Apache-2.0): `WinitView` adopts `UITextInput`, marked text becomes `Ime::Preedit`, a candidate or `unmarkText` becomes `Ime::Commit`. Changes on top of the PR (`ios/ime.rs` keeps its position/range classes, `ios/ime_document.rs` is new):
- The document UIKit sees is the text typed since the caret last moved plus the marked text (`ImeDocument`, UTF-16 offsets, the same design as macOS `ime_document.rs`), not only the marked text: that is what lets autocorrection (`replaceRange:withText:`, `textInRange:`) work. A replacement that reaches the caret becomes `Ime::Commit` with the replaced bytes available once from `WindowExtIOS::take_ime_delete_surrounding` (egui-winit forwards it as `DeleteSurroundingBytes`, like macOS/Wayland); ranges the document can't answer are ignored.
- The PR committed the old marked text on `setMarkedText:nil`: that turned Backspace on the last pinyin letter into a stray letter. Here nil/empty discards the composition; only `unmarkText` and a tap commit it. `insertText:` with a composition replaces it. Backspace in a composition edits only the composition.
- UTF-16 `NSRange` converted to UTF-8 offsets for `Preedit` (the PR used scalar counts).
- `Window::set_ime_cursor_area` positions `firstRectForRange:`/`caretRectForPosition:`; `set_ime_purpose(Password)` sets `isSecureTextEntry`, no autocorrection, and the document stays empty; `reset_ime`/`reset_ime_with_request` and `set_ime_allowed` drop the composition without committing (field change) and notify the `UITextInputDelegate`.
- Host test of the document model: `tests/ios_ime_document.rs`. egui-winit: `ime_delete_surrounding` has an iOS branch.
- `ImeDocument::delete_backward` also treats U+20D0-20FF (keycap, enclosing marks) and U+E0020-E007F (emoji tags, subregional flags) as cluster parts: egui deletes the whole grapheme, so the document forgets instead of dropping one scalar. Tests with surrogate pairs, ZWJ, keycap, tags, CJK and RTL neighbours in `ime_document.rs`; run with `cd vendor/winit-a517b38 && cargo test --test ios_ime_document` (winit is not a workspace member: no `--locked`).
Drop it when a winit release contains #4592 and an equivalent of the autocorrection link.

## Local patch: iOS edit menu, paste/copy/cut/select all, no secure flag towards UIKit
- `WinitView` answers the responder actions `paste:`, `copy:`, `cut:`, `selectAll:` (+ `canPerformAction:withSender:`), so the system edit menu and the hardware Cmd+C/X/V/A work in every egui text field. `paste:` reads `UIPasteboard.general.string` (the system menu is the sanctioned paste path: no iOS 16 paste prompt) and feeds it through `handle_insert_text`, i.e. exactly like typing (password included). `copy:`/`cut:` send the named keys Copy/Cut, `selectAll:` sends Cmd+A (`ModifiersChanged(SUPER)` + `A`); egui copies into `UIPasteboard` itself (egui-winit `clipboard.rs`). Copy/Cut are not offered in a password field.
- A `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` and a double `UITapGestureRecognizer` (touches are neither cancelled nor delayed: egui keeps them) present a `UIEditMenuInteraction` at the touch, only while a field has the focus (`ime_allowed`) and the touch is within 60 pt of the caret rectangle. After Select All the menu is shown again (as iOS does). Features added to the winit `objc2-ui-kit` list: `UIEditMenuInteraction`, `UIInteraction`, `UILongPressGestureRecognizer`, `UIPasteboard`.
- `isSecureTextEntry` is always false towards UIKit. Measured in the simulator: once UIKit has seen it true on this single view, the Passwords AutoFill bar stays on every later field (Matrix ID, chat composer) even after `reloadInputViews`, resign/become and an explicit `textContentType`. A password field keeps `ime_secure` (no autocorrection, no learning, empty document) but a third-party keyboard is allowed there. To get the system secure keyboard back, give the password field its own UIView.

## Local patch: iOS Passwords AutoFill on the sign-in form
- `ImePurpose` has three more values: `Username`, `Url`, `LoginPassword` (Wayland maps them to Normal/Password; the other backends ignore them). The mapping purpose -> UIKit traits is the pure `ios/ime_traits.rs` (host test `tests/ios_ime_traits.rs`: `cd vendor/winit-a517b38 && cargo test --test ios_ime_traits`, no `--locked`).
- The main `WinitView` never reports `isSecureTextEntry` true (that made the Passwords bar stick to every later field) and sets `textContentType` only to URL for the Server field; every other field leaves it nil.
- While a sign-in field (Matrix ID / Password) has the focus, two real, nearly invisible `UITextField`s (`WinitAutofillField`, content type username / password, the password one secure) are added to the view and the matching one becomes first responder instead of the view (`become_input_responder`); they are removed when another purpose takes the focus. UIKit decides AutoFill per first responder, so the composer, search and the rest keep the plain keyboard. The fields forward single typed characters, delete, paste/copy/cut/select-all to the main view; `pointInside` is false, so egui keeps every touch. UIKit's setters for `UITextContentType`/`secure` can't be sent to a `UITextField` from objc2 (runtime-resolved: "method not found"), so the traits are overridden in the subclass.
- A whole value inserted in one go (more than one character: Passwords AutoFill) is not typed: it goes to `platform::ios::take_autofill_credentials()` -> `(username, password)`; egui-winit puts it in egui's data store under `winit_autofill_credentials` and the sign-in form replaces the field.
- The traits applied on each focus change are logged permanently with NSLog (`gnobbi ime traits: <purpose> -> <traits>`); AutoFill fills log `gnobbi autofill fields: username|password N chars`.
- Routing (second round): typed characters never touch the hidden field's own text (nothing stale piles up); a whole value inserted by `insertText:` or `setText:` schedules `gnobbiCollect` 0.1 s later, which reads BOTH hidden fields, routes each to its own sign-in field with `ime_traits::split_autofill` (a password value that starts with the username, the observed concatenation, loses that prefix; a password equal to the username is dropped) and empties both. Lengths only are logged: `gnobbi autofill fields: username proxy N chars, password proxy M chars -> username N chars, password M chars`. The fields are stacked (username y 0, password y 40) and also get real UIKit traits (`setTextContentType:` / `setSecureTextEntry:` through raw `objc_msgSend`, the checked `msg_send!` refuses them in debug). Debug builds only: `GNOBBI_AF_INJECT=<text>` inserts that value into the password field once, 25 s after the fields exist (AutoFill of username + password together, which the simulator never produces).
- Simulator (iOS 26.5, iPhone 17, saved credential with username + password, Passwords key on the keyboard): one pick fills ONE field (username on Matrix ID; password only on Password): stacking, alpha 0.02 / 0.5 / 1, 200x44 or 300x44 fields and real traits did not change that. UIKit pair-fill is not obtainable here.
- Limits: AutoFill fills the focused field only (pick the entry once per field, not both at once); no "Save Password?" prompt can be relied on (see docs); the credential list for arbitrary homeservers appears through the keyboard's key button, there is no associated domain.
